data.title: Streptomycin
data.summary: Antituberculous drugs · Aminoglycoside antibiotic (first aminoglycoside); injectable antituberculous drug
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antituberculous drugs_

**Class:** Aminoglycoside antibiotic (first aminoglycoside); injectable antituberculous drug

## Mechanism of action
- Binds the 30S ribosomal subunit → misreading of mRNA → bactericidal for extracellular bacilli

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- TB (now rarely; previously in retreatment regimens)
- Plague, tularaemia, brucellosis (with doxycycline)
- Donovanosis and mycetoma (historical/alternative regimens)

## Dose & formulations
- 15 mg/kg IM daily (max 1 g; 0.75 g in older patients)

## Adverse effects
- Ototoxicity — mainly vestibular (vertigo, ataxia), also hearing loss
- Nephrotoxicity (less than other aminoglycosides), neuromuscular blockade
- Hypersensitivity rashes, contact dermatitis in health workers handling it

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy (fetal deafness), myasthenia gravis, pre-existing hearing/vestibular disease

## Drug interactions
- Other ototoxic/nephrotoxic drugs (loop diuretics, vancomycin, amphotericin B)

## Monitoring
- Hearing, balance, renal function

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (old FDA category D — congenital deafness).

## Viva points
- Vestibular toxicity — the classic streptomycin side effect
- Contraindicated in pregnancy

_Sources: Khopkar ch.7; Wolverton 4e ch.9 (aminoglycosides). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
